title: Gardenlet: lightweight admin utility surface + deterministic runbook taskifier
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Oncall and first-line support need a single, minimal surface for common admin actions (user resets, capacity nudges, model fallback triggers) that runs as deterministic tasks with idempotency guarantees. Current runbooks are long text docs or ad-hoc scripts which are hard to test and unsafe for non-privileged engineers.

Goal: Ship Gardenlet — a compact admin utility surface that converts approved runbook steps into typed, idempotent tasks executable from the Console and CLI. Gardenlet must: 1) be safe for staged access (RBAC), 2) produce structured audit events for compliance, 3) support dry-run rehearse mode, and 4) integrate with existing runbook telemetry and rollback primitives.

Non‑goals: full runbook DSL, replacing the large runbook compiler (this is a pragmatic surface and task library focused on 8–12 high-value ops actions).

Design highlights and tradeoffs:
- Deterministic tasks: tasks are small functions with explicit input schemas; we prefer typed validation over freeform scripts to reduce blast radius.
- Execution model: tasks run as controlled jobs in the operator service rather than arbitrary lambdas to preserve provenance and quota accounting.
- Safety tradeoff: to accelerate delivery we will restrict Gardenlet actions to a curated whitelist and require a gated approval flow for adding new actions.
- Observability: each task emits structured telemetry events (start/end/status/affected-resources) and attaches human-readable rationale to audit logs.

Success metrics: 50% reduction in mean time to remediate common incidents covered by Gardenlet actions; zero unintended escalations in first 90 days; 95% of Gardenlet executions include rationale and pass schema validation.
comments: 2025-02-16: Kickoff sync with PM and SRE. Agreed scope: 10 top ops actions from postmortem corpus. PM to prioritize list.
2025-02-20: Prototyped 'capacity-bump' and 'model-fallback' tasks. Initial CLI shim and Console button mocked in Figma (link below).
2025-02-25: Security review triage: KMS usage for any sensitive params required; RBAC gating must use existing SSO groups. Submitted initial SR ticket SR-1123.
2025-02-27: Review feedback from SRE: require dry-run with simulated side effects for dangerous steps. Added a DRY_RUN flag and rehearsal harness in prototype.
2025-03-01: PR opened for task runner core: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-gardenlet/pull/42. Integration tests failing on concurrency edge. Investigating lock scope.

2025-03-02: Blocker identified: operator job scheduler doesn't expose per-job IAM impersonation. Raised dependency ENG-247500. Temporary workaround: proxy executor with scoped tokens (requires hardened audit trail).
acceptance_criteria: A typed task SDK is available for creating Gardenlet actions with input schema validation and idempotency tokens.
Console UX: a single Gardenlet action panel with run/dry-run logs, rationale field, and required approval flow for privileged actions.
All executions emit structured telemetry and write an audit event containing actor, inputs, outcome, and rationale.
Whitelist mechanism: only approved actions listed in a curated registry may be executed; adding requires PR + security signoff.
End-to-end test coverage for dry-run, replay, and failure rollback semantics.
Documented runbook-to-task conversion guide for oncall and SRE (Confluence link included).
tasks: T1: Finalize canonical list of 10 seed actions with PM and SRE
T2: Implement task SDK (validation, idempotency token, result schema)
T3: Build operator-side executor with audit events and quota check
T4: Console panel prototype and CLI integration for invoking tasks
T5: Dry-run rehearsal harness that simulates side effects and captures diffs
T6: Security gating: KMS integration for secrets + RBAC enforcement
T7: End-to-end tests and chaos scenarios for concurrency and partial failures
T8: Docs, runbook conversion guide, and runbook-author training session
